![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/a8345270e511644cfb019099b907ecadff056f7efbd396e84d4313f3c3ab5817.png)

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(3)$ where $h(x)=f(x)-2g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)-2{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(3)={f}^{′}(3)-2{g}^{′}(3).
$$

Also, notice that $x=3$ corresponds to

- the interval $x\in (2,4)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (0,4)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/09e4836acd54b814c1691c60003614d206fc2eee5cda6d7ad8d6222dd72d2d4f.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (2,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{-2-2}{4-2}=-2.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(3)=-2.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (0,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{-2-0}{4-0}=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(3)=-\frac{1}{2}.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(3) & ={f}^{′}(3)-2{g}^{′}(3) \\  & =-2-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
